events_chronological: As a boy in Hollow Creek, Errol Doone looks into the eye of the witch in the swamp and sees how he will die, and so knows he will survive everything before it.
Errol grows into the town's champion at everything and saves Hollow Creek from the giant Torvald by befriending him.
Errol and Torvald leave together and part at a fork in the road, Errol taking the hard path through the woods.
Errol stumbles into a hidden town called Willow, where nobody wears shoes and nobody ever leaves, and meets a little girl called Pella.
Errol leaves Willow anyway and joins the ringmaster Grubb's circus, working three years unpaid for one fact a month about a girl he glimpsed across the tent.
Errol learns the girl is Marguerite, fills a field with daffodils for her, and takes a beating from her fiance Byrne.
Errol marries Marguerite and is drafted into the war, where he steals secret papers and is carried home by a pair of conjoined singers.
Reported dead, Errol walks back into Marguerite's life, and Byrne drops dead of a heart attack.
Errol becomes a travelling salesman away from home for weeks at a time and robs a bank with the poet Lomax.
Errol tells his tall tales at his son Sam's birth and at every family occasion afterwards.
Errol hijacks Sam's wedding reception with the story of catching the uncatchable catfish using his own wedding ring as bait.
Humiliated, Sam stops speaking to his father for three years.
Errol goes back to Willow, finds it derelict and repossessed, buys the town to save it, and meets the grown Pella.
Sam, living abroad with his pregnant wife Ilse, is told by his mother that Errol is dying.
Sam comes home and tries to get one true story out of his father, who will only tell the same tales.
Sam finds the deed to Willow among the papers and drives out to meet Pella, who tells him the truth: Errol never left Marguerite.
Errol has a stroke, and from his hospital bed he asks Sam to tell him how he dies.
Sam invents an ending in which he carries his father to the river and Errol turns into a great silver fish and swims away, and Errol dies happy.
At the funeral every character from the stories turns up, ordinary and real, and Sam sees how much of it was true after all.
Sam tells the same stories to his own small son by the river.
nonlinear_category_reason: The son's return to his dying father is the present, and the tall tales are flashbacks the father narrates.
syuzhet_notes: The frame is a son's return to his dying father. Told-order bullets 1-3 are a prologue of childhood and wedding-day memories, and bullets 6-14 are the father's tall tales, flashbacks he narrates and the film stages at face value with no marker that they are unreliable. Bullet 15 is a flashback the son assembles from documents rather than from his father, and the last five bullets return to the present.
fabula_notes: Most of the flashbacks are the father's embroidered version rather than what happened, and the film shows them as told; the funeral is what reveals which characters were real. The salesman years are compressed into a montage, and the father's decline happens between the son's visits.

events.content: The boys dare each other as far as the porch. Only one of them looks into the glass eye, and what he sees there is the last minute of his own life, which makes every minute before it survivable.
events.location: a shack in the swamp outside Hollow Creek

reader: intro:Errol
intro:the witch
he is fearless because he thinks he knows the ending

events.content: The town is losing sheep and sending men with torches. He walks up to the giant on his own and works out that the problem is not appetite but that there is nothing here big enough for him.

Torvald: somebody has spoken to him rather than at him
reader: intro:Torvald
his method is to talk to the monster

events.content: They leave together and the track splits, one way flat and long and the other straight through the woods. He takes the woods, because a story about the flat road is not worth telling.
events.location: a fork in the road out of Hollow Creek

reader: he chooses the version that will make a better account

events.content: He comes out of the woods with his boots gone into a town where the grass is cut short, nobody wears shoes and nobody has ever needed to leave. A small girl tells him he is early.

reader: intro:Pella
the place he is told he will come back to

events.content: He leaves anyway, and signs on with a ringmaster who pays him nothing and gives him, once a month, one fact about a girl he saw for three seconds across a crowded tent.

reader: intro:Grubb
three years bought a name, a flower and a hometown

events.content: He learns her name at last, empties every florist in the state, and stands in a yellow field asking her to marry him while her fiance hits him and he does not put his hands up.

Marguerite: someone has spent three years on her
reader: intro:Marguerite
intro:Byrne
he wins her by being unembarrassable

events.content: A wedding, and then a uniform. Behind the lines he takes papers off a desk that is not his, and is carried out of the country by a pair of singers joined at the hip.
events.location: a chapel and a foreign theatre

reader: the marriage and the war are one movement in his account

events.content: The telegram has already been delivered. He walks up the path anyway, and across town the man who was going to marry her puts a hand on his chest and sits down and does not get up.
events.location: the front path of Marguerite's house

reader: the rival is disposed of by the story rather than by him

events.content: Weeks at a time in other towns, a sample case in the boot, and one night a bank robbery with a poet who has run out of ways to say what he means.

reader: intro:Lomax
he is absent for most of the marriage, and it is all made into anecdote

events.content: He is not in the room. He is in a river, or a bar, depending which year he is telling it in, and the fish he catches is the size of the boy being born.
events.location: a hospital, and a river in the telling

Sam: the first of the stories, before he can object to it
reader: intro:Sam
the son's own birth reaches him as a tall tale

questions.q1: where do these stories come from, and why will he not stop?
questions.q8: were any of these people real?

events.content: He stands up at his son's reception with a glass and tells the room about the uncatchable fish and the gold ring he used as bait, and the room loves it, and his son does not.

Sam: his father will take any room, including this one
reader: intro:Ilse
the grievance, in its clearest form

questions.q2: what is the ring in the fish story?

events.content: Three years of not calling. There is no scene and no ultimatum; there is a number that does not get dialled and a father who keeps telling the story anyway.

reader: the estrangement is silence rather than argument

questions.q3: why does the son find his father unbearable?
questions.q7: will the two of them be reconciled before it is too late?

events.content: He goes back and finds it boarded and repossessed, so he buys the whole town off the bank and hands it back to the people in it. The girl who told him he was early is grown up now.

reader: the one large thing he did that he never made a story of

events.content: A telephone in a flat in another country, a pregnant wife in the next room, and a mother saying the word that ends the three years in one syllable.

reader: the clock the frame runs on

questions.q4: what has the old man been doing with himself?

events.content: He sits by the bed and asks, without much hope, for one thing that actually happened. He gets the giant, and the town in the woods, and the fish, told exactly as they always were.

reader: the son's demand, which the film will answer sideways

questions.q6: which parts of the stories actually happened?

events.content: He finds a deed among the papers, drives out to a town that turns out to exist, and is told by a woman who loved his father that nothing ever happened, because he never left his wife.

Sam: the story with the most obvious lie in it was the truest thing about him
reader: the answer arrives from a document, not from the father

events.content: The stroke takes most of his speech. What he can still do is ask his son, who has never made anything up in his life, to tell him how this one finishes.

reader: the handover: the teller asks to be told

events.content: He carries his father out through a corridor of everyone in the stories, down to the river, and puts him into the water, and a very large silver fish goes away downstream.

Errol: his son can do it too
reader: the death he saw in the eye, delivered by the person who doubted it

events.content: The giant is a tall man with a bad back. The ringmaster is short and sells insurance. The joined singers are sisters who stand close together. All of them came.

Sam: they were all real, and only the sizes were wrong
reader: how much of it was true, shown rather than argued

events.content: A river, a small boy, and a man who has finally worked out what the stories were for, saying the words in the order his father said them.

reader: the son becomes the teller, which is the only immortality on offer
